title: tb-scaffold.json contract (post-materialize)
description: Structural contract for asic/<module>/Verification/simulation-plan/tb-scaffold.json, validated at the sim-plan Completion Gate AFTER the materialize-scaffold verb has run. The sequence roster and the power scenarios live in their own files (sequences.json / power-scenarios.json) because their consumers differ; what remains here is what simulation alone reads. Strongly validates LLM-authored fields; tolerates (does not deep-validate) the interface/transaction objects materialize-scaffold injects into agents[] (their content is owned by materialize-scaffold + sim/_guards._agent_io). Referential integrity (observer/inports/seqs resolving to declared agents, and sequences.json/power-scenarios.json resolving against each other) is NOT expressible here; the check-scaffold gate's semantic layer enforces it.

feature.description: The features.json id this test exercises. Required: it is the key materialize-scaffold resolves feature_name through, and the only thing that makes a result traceable.

test_id.description: Stable per-test identifier; the regression log keys results by it.

suites.description: Which suites run this test. YOUR judgment as the plan author, not a script's: `make smoke` runs the smoke set, `make regress` runs everything. A smoke test is one whose failure means the design is broken badly enough that running the rest is pointless — pick them by that, not by position in the list.

feature_name.description: Script-injected by `simplan materialize-scaffold` (never hand-authored): the matching features.json entry's `name`, verbatim. It is what the Feature column of case-results-summary.md prints, so a human reads this rather than a bare id.

inports.description: The agents[].name values whose monitor streams feed the RM — one analysis_imp port each. Name the AGENT, not its transaction type: render-scaffold builds the type as <module>_<agent>_txn where it needs one, so a name written here in txn form would have to be un-wrapped and re-wrapped to reach the same string.

observer.description: The ONE agents[].name whose monitor stream the scoreboard compares against the RM. Omitted only when a single agent is declared; with more than one, omitting it is ambiguous and the gate rejects it.

intent.description: What this testpoint drives and why — the stimulus/intent the env and conformance-fix children read as the intent source. Distinct from the checks: `inlined_check_hints` says how each covered check is verified, this says what situation is being created.

covers.description: The `check-hints/<child>.json` check_ids this testpoint verifies. Present with an explicit empty array on a scenario testpoint you invented — omitted and `[]` are not the same claim, and an empty one traces to no feature.

inlined_check_hints.description: Script-injected by `simplan materialize-scaffold` (never hand-authored): the precise check semantics from the authored `check-hints/<child>.json`, materialized into this testpoint via its `covers[]`. `implementation_detail` is verbatim-if-present-else-summary. The feature a testpoint traces to is NOT copied in: the plan-review reviewer resolves it from covers[] + the authored check hints, both of which it already reads.
